definitions.gloss: unable to read the room, socially oblivious
definitions.explanation: A slang abbreviation for {空気|くうき}が{読|よ}めない (kuuki ga yomenai - can't read the atmosphere). Describes someone who fails to pick up on social cues or says inappropriate things in a given situation.

examples.japanese: {彼|かれ}はKYだから{場|ば}の{空気|くうき}を{壊|こわ}すことがある。
examples.english: He can't read the room, so he sometimes ruins the atmosphere.

examples.japanese: KYな{発言|はつげん}で{場|ば}が{凍|こお}った。
examples.english: The room went silent after that socially oblivious comment.

examples.japanese: 「KY」という{言葉|ことば}は2000{年代|ねんだい}に{流行|りゅうこう}した。
examples.english: The term 'KY' became popular in the 2000s.

notes:
ETYMOLOGY: Abbreviation of {空気|くうき} (K) + {読|よ}めない (Y), meaning "can't read the air/atmosphere." The term became widely popular around 2007 and was a top buzzword in Japan that year.

REGISTER: Casual/Slang
Primarily used in casual conversation. The abbreviation style reflects Japanese youth culture's tendency to create alphabet-based slang.

USAGE AS NA-ADJECTIVE:
・KYな{人|ひと} (a person who can't read the room)
・KYな{発言|はつげん} (a socially oblivious remark)
・KYな{行動|こうどう} (oblivious behavior)

RELATED EXPRESSIONS:
・{空気|くうき}を{読|よ}む (to read the room - positive ability)
・{空気|くうき}が{読|よ}めない (can't read the room - full form)
・{場|ば}の{空気|くうき} (the atmosphere of a place/situation)

CULTURAL NOTE:
The concept of {空気|くうき}を{読|よ}む reflects the importance of nonverbal communication and social harmony in Japanese culture. Being unable to do so (KY) is seen as a significant social deficiency.
